posts.title: The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate
posts.summary:
Is it better to cram more compute into each rack or rethink the architecture?
The post The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Hyperscalers including Google, Meta, and Microsoft are collaborating via the OCP 'Mount Diablo' project to standardize 1-megawatt rack architectures.
The transition to 1-megawatt racks necessitates a fundamental shift where the rack is treated as an integrated compute system rather than a passive enclosure.
Key technical hurdles include managing extreme power density, liquid cooling requirements, and the physical limitations of copper connectivity for high-lane-count AI systems.
Industry experts are debating whether extreme rack density is a necessary evolution for AI workloads or if distributed, fragmented architectures might offer a more efficient alternative.

posts.title: Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip
posts.summary:
As AI clusters push beyond rack-scale limits, optical interconnects and circuit switching are reshaping how data centers scale. 
The post Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The traditional distinction between copper-based 'scale-up' and optical 'scale-out' is blurring as copper reaches physical limits regarding signal loss and power consumption.
Optical interconnects are increasingly penetrating the rack-scale domain to address latency issues that currently leave GPUs underutilized at roughly 25% efficiency.
New scaling terminology is emerging, including 'scale-in,' which refers to the bandwidth capacity maintained within a single chassis as clusters grow beyond individual racks.
Major players like Google are adopting optical circuit switching (OCS) in torus configurations to overcome the bandwidth and distance constraints of traditional electrical signaling.

posts.title: What Will It Take To Deploy CPO At Scale?
posts.summary:
The path to widespread deployment of co-packaged optics depends on solving challenges in manufacturing, testing, and operations.
The post What Will It Take To Deploy CPO At Scale? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Co-packaged optics (CPO) are transitioning from prototypes to production, initially targeting scale-out switch ASICs where copper bandwidth is insufficient.
Widespread adoption of CPO for 'scale-up' networks—where thousands of XPUs must communicate with minimal latency—remains the next major technical hurdle.
Commercial success for CPO depends on maturing the entire ecosystem, specifically addressing manufacturing, testing, and supply chain reliability for high-volume deployment.
Industry leaders are focused on standardizing wavelength multiplication and port density to ensure CPO can support multi-generational scaling for AI infrastructure.

posts.title: Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash
posts.summary: The police-tech giant Flock is announcing today that it will change officers’ access to its nationwide network of license plate readers, in an apparent effort to quell a growing backlash and win back contracts lost amid concerns about mass surveillance and police abuse. Several changes aim directly at a problem that has made recent headlines:…
bullets: Flock is mandating that officers input a criminal case number for all searches, a response to a Washington Post investigation identifying 46 instances of police using the 120,000-camera network for unauthorized stalking.
The company is making its automatic auditing system mandatory to flag suspicious search patterns, though the tool's accuracy remains unverified by independent third parties.
To mitigate privacy concerns, Flock now recommends that agencies reduce data retention periods from 30 days to seven days, though this remains an optional setting for local departments.

Despite new guardrails, critics argue the system remains vulnerable to abuse because Flock does not verify the validity of entered case numbers, allowing officers to bypass safeguards with placeholder text.

posts.title: BYD's flash charging Qin Max sedan goes on sale in China for under $15,000
posts.summary:
The BYD Qin Max is the flagship of the Qin family, available in EV and DM-i versions.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD has launched the Qin Max sedan, priced between 99,900 and 143,900 yuan, as a strategic move to revitalize its flagship Qin lineup following a significant sales decline this year.
The EV variant features BYD's second-generation Blade Battery and flash charging technology, enabling a 10% to 97% charge in just nine minutes.
The DM-i plug-in hybrid model achieves a class-leading fuel consumption of 2.59 liters per 100 km and offers an impressive combined range of 2,370 km.
The vehicle integrates advanced technology, including LiDAR-based 'God's Eye B' navigation assist and a built-in AI agent, targeting younger demographics to regain market share.
